Regulator response path.value: Chief Actuary coordinates the response with Tax Director and General Counsel

checklist.step: Scope the year's actuarial opinion coverage
actions: Confirm the legal entities, lines of business and reserve segments requiring an opinion for the current statutory annual statement.
Identify whether the opinion will be qualified as to any segment based on preliminary reserve adequacy indications.
Confirm the opinion type required (asset adequacy analysis opinion vs. formula reserve opinion) per the domiciliary state's regulation.
Document the scope decision in the opinion planning memo.
checklist.done: an opinion planning memo names every entity, line of business and opinion type required for the year.

checklist.step: Pull the year-end reserve data and confirm it reconciles to the annual statement
actions: Extract year-end statutory reserves by line of business and reserve segment from the actuarial modeling platform.
Reconcile the extract to the Exhibit 5/8/9 reserve totals in the draft statutory annual statement.
Resolve any unreconciled difference with the Statutory Reporting Manager before opinion work begins.
Document the reconciliation and file it with the opinion support.
checklist.done: reserve data used for the opinion reconciles to the draft annual statement exhibits.

checklist.step: Perform the asset adequacy analysis supporting the opinion
actions: Run the cash-flow-testing or gross premium valuation models required for each reserve segment under the domiciliary state's opinion requirements.
Test reserve adequacy under the required scenarios (interest rate scenarios, moderately adverse conditions) per the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice.
Identify any segment showing an adequacy shortfall and quantify the additional reserve needed.
Route results to the Appointed Actuary for review.
checklist.done: asset adequacy testing is complete for every reserve segment with any shortfall quantified and routed for review.

checklist.step: Reconcile the statutory reserve basis to the federal tax reserve basis
actions: Compare the statutory reserve figures underlying the opinion to the §807(d)(1) tax reserve computation prepared separately.
Confirm the applicable NAIC method used in the tax computation matches the method the opinion relies on for each contract form.
Document any intentional difference (e.g., the 92.81% haircut) so it is not mistaken for an error.
Route the reconciliation to the Appointed Actuary and Tax Director.
checklist.done: a documented reconciliation ties the opinion's statutory reserve basis to the tax reserve basis, explaining every intentional difference.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial opinion document
actions: Draft the opinion using the current NAIC Annual Statement Instructions opinion language template for the applicable opinion type.
State the scope, reserve amounts opined on, and the opinion conclusion (reserves make good and sufficient provision, or qualified language with the specific exception named).
Include the required actuarial standards of practice reference (ASOP 22 for asset adequacy, applicable ASOPs for formula reserves).
Route the draft to the Chief Actuary for technical review.
checklist.done: a draft opinion citing the correct scope, conclusion and ASOP references is ready for Chief Actuary review.

checklist.step: Draft the supporting actuarial memorandum
actions: Draft the memorandum per the Model #822 content checklist: reserve methodology, assumptions, data sources, testing methodology, and the sensitivity/scenario results.
Include a summary reconciling the memorandum's reserve figures to the opinion and to the annual statement exhibits.
Include disclosure of any Appointed Actuary reliance on other experts (e.g., an outside asset adequacy testing vendor) with their qualifications.
Route the draft memorandum to the Appointed Actuary for review.
checklist.done: a draft memorandum covering methodology, assumptions, results and reliance disclosures is ready for review.

checklist.step: Resolve any adequacy shortfall before the opinion is finalized
actions: Review any shortfall identified in adequacy testing with the Reserving Actuary and Tax Director.
Decide whether to strengthen reserves, adjust assumptions with documented support, or issue a qualified opinion disclosing the shortfall.
Document the decision rationale in the opinion working file.
Notify the CFO of any reserve strengthening that will affect the tax provision.
checklist.done: every identified shortfall has a documented resolution decision before the opinion is finalized.

checklist.step: Have an independent peer review the opinion and memorandum
actions: Assign a peer reviewer who did not participate in preparing the opinion or memorandum.
Confirm the reviewer checks the opinion language against the current NAIC template, the memorandum's completeness against the Model #822 checklist, and the reserve-to-exhibit reconciliation.
Log review comments and confirm each is resolved before finalization.
File the peer review sign-off with the opinion working papers.
checklist.done: a peer review is completed with all comments resolved and the sign-off filed.

checklist.step: Route the opinion and memorandum for Chief Actuary approval
actions: Review the final opinion and memorandum against the peer review comments and the shortfall resolution decision.
Confirm the reserve figures still tie to the final draft annual statement exhibits.
Approve the documents for the Appointed Actuary's signature or return with further comments.
Log the approval date.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has approved the final opinion and memorandum or returned them with documented comments.

checklist.step: Sign the actuarial opinion
actions: Sign and date the final actuarial opinion, confirming the signature date is on or before the statutory filing deadline.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary's credentials (FSA/MAAA membership status) are current as of the signature date.
File the signed opinion in the compliance evidence repository.
Notify the Statutory Reporting Manager that the signed opinion is ready for filing.
checklist.done: the opinion is signed, dated on or before the deadline, with current credentials confirmed and filed.

checklist.step: Finalize and file the memorandum ready for regulator request
actions: Finalize the memorandum incorporating all approved changes.
Confirm the memorandum is available to produce within the domiciliary state's required response timeframe (commonly 60 days) if requested.
File the finalized memorandum alongside the signed opinion in the compliance evidence repository.
Log the finalization date.
checklist.done: the finalized memorandum is filed and ready to produce within the regulator's required timeframe.

checklist.step: Communicate the opinion conclusion and any qualification to the Audit Committee
actions: Present the opinion conclusion, any qualification, and the shortfall resolution (if any) to the Audit Committee ahead of the statutory filing.
Answer committee questions on the reserve adequacy testing methodology.
Record the presentation and any committee direction in the board portal minutes.
File the minutes with the opinion working papers.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has been briefed on the opinion conclusion before filing, with minutes filed.

checklist.step: Provide the reconciled tax reserve basis to Tax for the provision
actions: Take the final reserve figures underlying the signed opinion and apply the §807(d)(1) 92.81%/net-surrender-value greater-of adjustment.
Load the resulting tax reserve into the tax provision workpaper.
Confirm the figure is consistent with the separately performed §807(d)(1) computation under the related control item.
Log the hand-off date to Tax.
checklist.done: the reconciled tax reserve figure is handed to Tax and loaded into the provision, consistent with the separate §807(d)(1) computation.

checklist.step: Retain the opinion and memorandum package for the required period
actions: Assemble the signed opinion, memorandum, peer review sign-off, adequacy testing results and Chief Actuary approval.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under the tax/statutory year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the package is indexed and retrievable by year and reserve segment.
checklist.done: the opinion and memorandum package is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by year and segment.

checklist.step: Track and close any post-filing regulator inquiry on the opinion
actions: Log any regulator follow-up question on the opinion or memorandum in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
Prepare and route the response through the Chief Actuary and General Counsel before submission.
Confirm the response is submitted within the regulator's requested timeframe.
File the closed inquiry with the opinion package.
checklist.done: every regulator inquiry on the opinion is logged, responded to within the requested timeframe, and filed.

testing.step: Build the population of reserve segments covered by the year's opinion
actions: Extract the list of reserve segments and contract forms covered by the signed opinion.
Reconcile the segment list to the statutory annual statement exhibits for completeness.
Resolve any segment missing from the opinion scope before sampling.
testing.done: the segment population reconciles to the annual statement exhibits and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Select 100% of segments representing more than 5% of total reserves.
Select a random, reproducible sample of remaining segments, minimum 5.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of material reserve segments.

testing.step: Re-perform the reserve-to-exhibit reconciliation for sampled segments
actions: Independently pull year-end reserves for each sampled segment from the actuarial modeling platform.
Compare to the amount disclosed in the memorandum and the annual statement exhibit.
Log any unreconciled difference as an exception.
testing.done: reserves for every sampled segment reconcile across the model, memorandum and exhibit, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Independently re-check the adequacy testing methodology and results
actions: Review the scenarios and assumptions used in the adequacy testing for each sampled segment against the requirements of the applicable ASOP.
Re-run a reduced-scenario version of the testing where feasible and compare directional results.
Confirm any disclosed shortfall's dollar amount and resolution are consistent with the memorandum.
Log any methodology gap or unreconciled shortfall as an exception.
testing.done: adequacy testing methodology and shortfall disclosure are independently checked for every sampled segment, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify the opinion signature date and Appointed Actuary credentials
actions: Confirm the signed opinion's date is on or before the statutory filing deadline for the tested year.
Verify the Appointed Actuary's FSA/MAAA membership status was current as of the signature date via the professional body's public directory.
Log any late signature or lapsed credential as an exception.
testing.done: the opinion signature date and credential status are verified for the tested year, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Confirm the reconciliation between the statutory and federal tax reserve basis
actions: Pull the reconciliation prepared between the opinion's statutory reserve and the §807(d)(1) tax reserve for sampled segments.
Independently recompute the 92.81%/net-surrender-value comparison for a sub-sample of contract forms within the segment.
Compare to the filed reconciliation and log any discrepancy.
testing.done: the statutory-to-tax reserve reconciliation is independently checked for sampled segments, or the discrepancy is logged.

testing.step: Verify peer review and Chief Actuary approval evidence
actions: Pull the peer review sign-off and Chief Actuary approval for the tested year.
Confirm the peer reviewer was independent of the opinion's preparation team.
Confirm approval dates pre-date the opinion signature date.
Log any missing or out-of-sequence approval as an exception.
testing.done: peer review and Chief Actuary approval are confirmed independent and pre-dated, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Confirm memorandum completeness against the Model #822 checklist
actions: Compare the finalized memorandum's contents section-by-section against the current Model #822 content checklist.
Flag any required section that is missing or materially incomplete.
Log the completeness result in the test workpaper.
testing.done: the memorandum's completeness is checked against the Model #822 checklist for the tested year, with any gap logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the segment, what was wrong, and the reserve/opinion impact.
Assign a root cause and an owner from the Actuarial team.
Set a remediation date and require any material finding be flagged to the Chief Actuary for opinion-impact assessment.
Carry every open exception into next cycle's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and mandatory retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and assess whether any exception would have changed the opinion conclusion.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the underlying workpapers.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled re-performance sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Chief Actuary and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Chief Actuary.

checklist.step: Confirm the signed actuarial opinion is ready before the annual statement is assembled
actions: Check with the Appointed Actuary that the signed opinion and memorandum are complete per the opinion sign-off tracker.
Confirm the opinion's signature date is on or before the intended annual statement submission date.
Pull the final signed opinion PDF into the annual statement assembly folder.
Flag any delay to the CFO immediately, since the annual statement cannot be filed without the attached opinion.
checklist.done: the signed opinion PDF is confirmed complete and staged in the annual statement assembly folder before submission.

checklist.step: Assemble the full statutory annual statement package
actions: Compile the Jurat page, all required exhibits and schedules, the signed actuarial opinion, and the general interrogatories into the filing package.
Cross-check the reserve figures in the exhibits against the figures underlying the signed opinion for consistency.
Run the NAIC's electronic filing validation checks and resolve any flagged edit failures before submission.
Route the assembled package to the CFO for final sign-off.
checklist.done: the full annual statement package, opinion attached, passes NAIC validation checks and has CFO sign-off.

checklist.step: Submit the annual statement with opinion to the domiciliary regulator
actions: Log in to the NAIC statutory filing system and upload the complete annual statement package including the attached signed opinion.
Submit the filing to the domiciliary state by the March 1 statutory deadline.
Download the submission confirmation/receipt and verify the opinion attachment is listed among the filed documents.
File the confirmation in the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the annual statement with opinion attached is submitted by March 1 and the confirmation lists the opinion as filed.

checklist.step: File copies with every additional state requiring the annual statement
actions: Pull the list of states requiring a copy filing from the holding company/annual statement filing requirement matrix.
Submit the identical package (with opinion) to each required state's filing channel.
Track submission status per state in the filing tracker.
Escalate any state rejecting the filing to the Regulatory Reporting Manager same-day.
checklist.done: the annual statement is filed with every required copy state, tracked to completion in the filing tracker.

checklist.step: Build the Form 1120-L return using the reconciled reserve and DAC figures
actions: Pull the final §807(d)(1) reserve figure and §848 DAC capitalization figure from the Tax team's computation workpapers.
Compute life insurance company taxable income (life insurance gross income less allowable deductions) per §801 and populate Form 1120-L and its supporting schedules.
Reconcile the return's reserve and income figures to the signed actuarial opinion and the audited financial statements.
Route the draft return to the Tax Director for review.
checklist.done: a draft Form 1120-L is built with reserve/DAC figures reconciled to the opinion and audited statements, ready for Tax Director review.

checklist.step: Review the draft return for consistency with the opinion and annual statement
actions: Compare the return's reported reserves line-by-line to the figures underlying the signed opinion.
Confirm the DAC capitalization and §831(b) positions (where elected) are consistent with the control computations performed earlier in the year.
Resolve any discrepancy with the Tax Manager before the return is finalized.
Sign off the reviewed return.
checklist.done: the Tax Director's review confirms consistency with the opinion and annual statement, with sign-off recorded.

checklist.step: Route the return for CFO and General Counsel review before filing
actions: Present the finalized return and its key positions (reserve method, DAC capitalization, any §831(b) election) to the CFO.
Have General Counsel review any position with elevated audit risk or uncertain tax position disclosure implications.
Obtain CFO sign-off to file.
Log the sign-off date.
checklist.done: CFO sign-off to file is obtained and logged before the return is submitted.

checklist.step: File Form 1120-L through the IRS Modernized e-File system
actions: Submit Form 1120-L and all supporting schedules through the IRS Modernized e-File (MeF) system by the due date, or file Form 7004 for an automatic extension beforehand.
Retain the e-file submission ID and the IRS acceptance acknowledgment.
If rejected, correct the identified error and resubmit within the IRS's resubmission window.
File the accepted acknowledgment in the filing tracker.
checklist.done: Form 1120-L is accepted by the IRS e-file system by the due date or extended due date, with the acknowledgment on file.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed return to the filed annual statement
actions: Build a line-by-line reconciliation of reserves, DAC and net income between the filed Form 1120-L and the filed annual statement exhibits.
Document every book-tax difference with its statutory basis.
Route the reconciliation to the Tax Director for sign-off.
File the signed reconciliation with both filings.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation ties the filed return to the filed annual statement, with every difference explained.

checklist.step: Confirm the opinion attachment and return filing dates satisfy every applicable deadline
actions: Compare the annual statement submission date and the Form 1120-L acceptance date against their respective statutory deadlines.
Confirm any extension filed (Form 7004, or a state's annual statement extension) is on file and was itself timely.
Log the confirmed compliance status in the filing tracker.
Notify the Tax Director and CFO of confirmed on-time status or of any exception.
checklist.done: on-time filing status (or a documented, timely-filed extension) is confirmed and logged for both filings.

checklist.step: Respond to any regulator or IRS follow-up on the filed opinion or return
actions: Log any follow-up inquiry received from a state DOI or the IRS in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
Route the inquiry to the Tax Director (for return matters) or the Appointed Actuary (for opinion matters) for a technical response.
Have General Counsel review the response before submission.
Submit the response within the regulator's stated timeframe and log the submission date.
checklist.done: every follow-up inquiry is logged, technically reviewed, and responded to within the regulator's timeframe.

checklist.step: Monitor for any post-filing amendment need
actions: Track any subsequent reserve restatement, opinion correction, or audit adjustment identified after the original filing.
Assess with the Tax Director whether an amended Form 1120-L or an amended annual statement filing is required.
Where required, prepare and file the amendment following the same review chain as the original filing.
Log the amendment and its filing date in the filing tracker.
checklist.done: any post-filing change is assessed for amendment need, and any required amendment is filed and logged.

checklist.step: Reconcile filing confirmations against the filing tracker at year end
actions: Pull every filing confirmation and e-file acknowledgment obtained during the year.
Cross-check each against the filing tracker's planned filing list to confirm nothing was missed.
Resolve any tracker entry without a matching confirmation before year-end close.
checklist.done: every planned filing has a matching confirmation on file, with no unresolved gap at year-end.

checklist.step: Retain the full filing package for the required period
actions: Assemble the filed annual statement, signed opinion, Form 1120-L, e-file acknowledgment, and the reserve/DAC reconciliation.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under the filing year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the package is indexed and retrievable by filing year and filing type.
checklist.done: the full filing package is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by year and filing type.

checklist.step: Certify overall filing completeness to the CFO
actions: Prepare a completeness certification listing every required filing for the year, its submission date, and confirmation status.
Present the certification to the CFO for sign-off.
File the signed certification with the filing package.
Communicate certification completion to the Audit Committee at its next scheduled meeting.
checklist.done: a CFO-signed completeness certification exists and is communicated to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: Build the population of required filings for the tax year
actions: Extract the full list of required annual statement filings (domiciliary plus copy states) and the Form 1120-L filing from the filing tracker.
Reconcile the extract to the holding company filing requirement matrix for completeness.
Resolve any unreconciled required filing before sampling.
testing.done: the filing population reconciles to the requirement matrix and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of the domiciliary annual statement filing and the Form 1120-L filing.
Take a random sample of at least 5 copy-state filings.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of the domiciliary and federal filings.

testing.step: Confirm the opinion was attached to every sampled annual statement filing
actions: Open the NAIC statutory filing system and pull the list of attached documents for each sampled filing.
Confirm the signed actuarial opinion appears among the attachments.
Confirm the opinion's signature date is on or before the filing submission date.
Log any missing attachment or out-of-sequence date as an exception.
testing.done: the opinion attachment and its date are verified for every sampled annual statement filing, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Verify each sampled filing was submitted by its statutory deadline
actions: Pull the submission timestamp for each sampled filing and compare to the March 1 (annual statement) or Form 1120-L due date/extended due date.
Confirm any extension claimed was itself filed timely.
Log any late filing without a timely extension as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled filing's timeliness is verified, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Trace the Form 1120-L reserve and DAC figures to the signed opinion and audited statements
actions: Pull the reserve and DAC figures reported on the filed Form 1120-L.
Trace them to the figures underlying the signed opinion and the audited financial statements.
Log any unexplained difference as an exception.
testing.done: Form 1120-L figures trace to the opinion and audited statements, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm the e-file acknowledgment reflects acceptance, not rejection
actions: Pull the IRS MeF acknowledgment for the sampled Form 1120-L filing.
Confirm the status is Accepted, not Rejected or Pending.
For any rejection, confirm a timely corrected resubmission and acceptance exists.
Log any unresolved rejection as an exception.
testing.done: acceptance is confirmed for the sampled return, or any rejection is confirmed timely resolved, else logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm CFO sign-off preceded each sampled filing
actions: Pull the CFO sign-off record for the return and the annual statement package.
Compare the sign-off date to the actual submission date.
Log any filing submitted before CFO sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: CFO sign-off pre-dates submission for every sampled filing, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Verify copy-state filings match the domiciliary package content
actions: Compare the sampled copy-state filing package to the domiciliary filing package for the same year.
Confirm the opinion and exhibit content are identical (allowing for state-specific cover sheets).
Log any material content difference as an exception.
testing.done: sampled copy-state filings match the domiciliary package content, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the filing, what was missed, and the regulatory impact.
Assign a root cause and an owner from the Regulatory Reporting team.
Set a remediation date and, for any late federal filing, assess penalty exposure with the Tax Director.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and mandatory retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missing-attachment and zero-late-filing thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the underlying workpapers.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled testing sign the workpaper.
Report results to the CFO and Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the CFO and Audit Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the asset adequacy analysis and cash-flow testing documentation supporting the actuarial opinion and the §807(d)(1) reserve basis it feeds into

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — testing scope checked against the NAIC Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation (Model #822) and ASOP 22 (Statements of Opinion Based on Asset Adequacy Analysis), cross-referenced to §807(d)(1) so tax reserve figures are consistent with the tested statutory basis

In-scope processes.value: Annual cash-flow testing / gross premium valuation across interest rate and moderately adverse scenarios for every reserve segment subject to asset adequacy analysis

In-scope systems.value: Cash-flow testing models run in the actuarial modeling platform; scenario assumptions and results archived in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Asset Adequacy Analysis / Cash-Flow Testing Procedure — segment scoping, scenario set construction, assumption-setting governance, documentation retention checklist per ASOP 22

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary; reviewed annually against the current ASOP 22 and Model #822 requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Testing must complete and be documented ahead of the March 1 actuarial opinion signature deadline that relies on its results

Deadline reminders configured.value: Testing milestone reminders at T-60/T-30/T-10 days before the opinion signature deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Cash-flow testing model files, assumption support, scenario results and the AAT report retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any segment failing adequacy testing without a documented resolution (reserve strengthening or qualified opinion) is logged as an exception

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off resolution of any adequacy shortfall before the opinion relying on the testing is signed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All reserve segments subject to asset adequacy analysis for the year, and the full scenario set run against each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any segment where the AAT report's documented scenario results cannot be reproduced from the underlying model file is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual, matching the Annual obligation frequency, tested against each year's AAT cycle

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual AAT documentation test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator response path.value: Chief Actuary coordinates the response with the Appointed Actuary and General Counsel

checklist.step: Scope the segments and scenario set for the year's cash-flow testing
actions: Confirm with the Appointed Actuary which reserve segments require asset adequacy analysis for the current opinion cycle.
Select the interest rate scenario set (the New York 7 scenarios or an equivalent stochastic set) and any additional moderately adverse scenarios per ASOP 22.
Document the scoping rationale, including any segment excluded and why.
Route the scoping memo to the Chief Actuary for approval before modeling begins.
checklist.done: an approved scoping memo names every tested segment and the scenario set to be applied.

checklist.step: Assemble and validate the asset and liability model inputs
actions: Extract the year-end asset portfolio (book/market value, cash flows, credit ratings) from the investment accounting system for the tested segments.
Extract the year-end policy liability data (reserves, cash flow projections, lapse/mortality/morbidity assumptions) from the actuarial modeling platform.
Reconcile total assets and liabilities loaded into the model to the general ledger and reserve exhibits.
Resolve any unreconciled difference before running scenarios.
checklist.done: asset and liability model inputs are loaded and reconciled to the GL and reserve exhibits for every tested segment.

checklist.step: Document and get sign-off on key actuarial assumptions
actions: Document the source and rationale for lapse, mortality, morbidity, expense and reinvestment/disinvestment assumptions used in the model.
Compare current-year assumptions to the prior year and explain any material change.
Route the assumption set to the Chief Actuary for sign-off before scenarios are run.
File the signed assumption memo with the testing documentation.
checklist.done: assumptions are documented, changes from the prior year explained, and Chief Actuary sign-off obtained before scenarios run.

checklist.step: Run the full scenario set for each tested segment
actions: Execute each interest rate and moderately adverse scenario against the loaded assets and liabilities for every tested segment.
Confirm model runs complete without error and produce the projected surplus/deficiency by scenario and duration.
Save the run output files with a version-controlled naming convention in the model governance repository.
Flag any scenario producing a projected deficiency for review.
checklist.done: every scenario is run for every segment with output files version-controlled and any deficiency flagged.

checklist.step: Analyze results and identify any reserve adequacy shortfall
actions: Review the projected surplus/deficiency results across all scenarios for each segment.
Identify the worst-case scenario result and compare against the segment's held reserve.
Where a deficiency is projected, quantify the additional reserve amount needed to eliminate it.
Route the analysis to the Chief Actuary and Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: results are analyzed for every segment with any shortfall quantified and routed for review.

checklist.step: Decide the resolution for any identified shortfall
actions: Review the shortfall quantification with the Valuation Actuary and Tax Director.
Decide whether to strengthen statutory reserves, refine assumptions with documented support, or accept a qualified opinion for the segment.
Document the decision rationale in the AAT working file.
Notify the CFO of any reserve strengthening's impact on the tax provision.
checklist.done: every identified shortfall has a documented resolution decision approved by the Chief Actuary.

checklist.step: Draft the AAT report documenting methodology, assumptions and results
actions: Draft the AAT report covering scope, methodology, scenario set, assumptions, results by segment and any shortfall resolution.
Include enough detail that an independent actuary could reproduce the results from the report and the underlying model files.
Cross-reference the report's reserve figures to the annual statement exhibits and the actuarial opinion.
Route the draft to the Chief Actuary for review.
checklist.done: a draft AAT report with reproducible methodology detail is ready for Chief Actuary review.

checklist.step: Have an independent peer reviewer check the AAT report and model files
actions: Assign a reviewer who did not build the models or set the assumptions under review.
Confirm the reviewer can reproduce the reported worst-case scenario result from the archived model file.
Log review comments and confirm each is resolved before the report is finalized.
File the peer review sign-off with the AAT documentation.
checklist.done: a peer review confirms reproducibility and all comments are resolved before finalization.

checklist.step: Finalize and approve the AAT report
actions: Review the final AAT report against the peer review comments and the shortfall resolution decision.
Confirm the report's reserve figures still tie to the final annual statement exhibits.
Approve the report for use as opinion support.
Log the approval date.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary approves the finalized AAT report before it is used to support the opinion.

checklist.step: Hand the AAT results to the Appointed Actuary for the opinion
actions: Provide the approved AAT report and its conclusion to the Appointed Actuary ahead of opinion drafting.
Confirm the opinion's reserve adequacy language matches the AAT report's conclusion.
Flag any inconsistency for resolution before the opinion is signed.
checklist.done: the AAT report is handed to the Appointed Actuary and its conclusion matches the opinion language before signature.

checklist.step: Version-control and archive the model files used to produce the reported results
actions: Lock and archive the final model files (input data, assumption tables, scenario definitions, output) used to produce the reported results.
Tag the archive with the tax/statutory year and segment.
Confirm the archived files are read-only and cannot be altered after archiving.
Log the archive location in the AAT documentation.
checklist.done: final model files are locked, archived read-only, and logged against the AAT documentation.

checklist.step: Reconcile AAT reserve figures to the §807(d)(1) tax reserve computation
actions: Compare the reserve figures underlying the AAT report to the separately computed §807(d)(1) tax reserve for the same segments.
Confirm the applicable NAIC method and any intentional adjustment (the 92.81% factor) are consistently applied.
Document any discrepancy and route it to the Valuation Actuary and Tax Director for resolution.
checklist.done: AAT and tax reserve figures are reconciled with any discrepancy documented and resolved.

checklist.step: Present the AAT results and any shortfall resolution to the Audit Committee
actions: Present the year's AAT scope, results and any shortfall resolution to the Audit Committee ahead of opinion signature.
Answer committee questions on methodology and assumption changes.
Record the presentation in the board portal minutes.
File the minutes with the AAT documentation.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee is briefed on AAT results before the opinion is signed, with minutes filed.

checklist.step: Retain the AAT documentation package for the required period
actions: Assemble the scoping memo, assumption sign-off, scenario output, AAT report, peer review sign-off and archived model file references.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under the tax/statutory year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the package is indexed and retrievable by year and segment.
checklist.done: the AAT documentation package is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by year and segment.

checklist.step: Confirm the documentation can be produced within the regulator's requested timeframe
actions: Confirm the archived model files can be reopened and rerun without error as a readiness check.
Confirm the AAT report and supporting workpapers are indexed for rapid retrieval.
Log the readiness check date and outcome in the AAT documentation.
Notify the Chief Actuary of any readiness gap for remediation before the next request cycle.
checklist.done: a readiness check confirms the AAT package can be produced within the regulator's requested timeframe, logged for the year.

testing.step: Build the population of tested segments and scenario runs for the year
actions: Extract the list of segments and the full scenario set run for the year from the AAT documentation.
Reconcile the segment list to the scoping memo and the annual statement exhibits.
Resolve any unreconciled segment or scenario before sampling.
testing.done: the tested-segment population reconciles to the scoping memo and exhibits, signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Select 100% of segments where the AAT report disclosed a shortfall or a qualification.
Select a random, reproducible sample of remaining segments, minimum 3.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of segments with a disclosed shortfall or qualification.

testing.step: Reproduce the worst-case scenario result from the archived model file
actions: Reopen the archived, locked model file for each sampled segment.
Rerun the worst-case scenario identified in the AAT report without changing any input.
Compare the reproduced result to the figure reported in the AAT report.
Log any inability to reproduce or any material variance as an exception.
testing.done: the worst-case result is reproduced from the archived model for every sampled segment, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Verify assumption sign-off and change documentation
actions: Pull the assumption memo and Chief Actuary sign-off for each sampled segment.
Confirm any assumption change from the prior year has a documented rationale.
Confirm the sign-off date pre-dates the scenario run date.
Log any missing sign-off or unexplained change as an exception.
testing.done: assumption sign-off and change documentation are verified for every sampled segment, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Confirm asset and liability inputs reconcile to source records
actions: Pull the asset and liability data loaded into the sampled segment's model.
Independently trace total assets to the investment accounting system and total liabilities to the reserve exhibit.
Log any unreconciled difference as an exception.
testing.done: model inputs reconcile to source records for every sampled segment, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify shortfall resolution decisions were properly authorized
actions: Pull the Chief Actuary's resolution decision for every sampled segment with a disclosed shortfall.
Confirm the resolution (reserve strengthening, assumption refinement, or qualified opinion) was implemented as decided.
Log any undocumented or unimplemented resolution as an exception.
testing.done: every disclosed shortfall's resolution is confirmed authorized and implemented, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify peer review evidence and reviewer independence
actions: Pull the peer review sign-off for each sampled segment.
Confirm the reviewer named did not build the model or set assumptions for that segment.
Confirm review comments logged were resolved before finalization.
Log any independence conflict or unresolved comment as an exception.
testing.done: peer review independence and comment resolution are confirmed for every sampled segment, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Reconcile AAT reserve figures to the §807(d)(1) tax reserve and the opinion
actions: Independently compare the AAT report's reserve figures for sampled segments to the §807(d)(1) tax reserve computation and the signed opinion.
Confirm consistency, allowing for the documented 92.81% adjustment.
Log any unexplained inconsistency as an exception.
testing.done: AAT, tax reserve and opinion figures are consistent for every sampled segment, or the inconsistency is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the segment, what was wrong, and the reserve/opinion impact.
Assign a root cause and an owner from the Actuarial team.
Set a remediation date and require any non-reproducible result be flagged to the Chief Actuary for opinion-impact assessment.
Carry every open exception into next cycle's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and mandatory retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and assess whether any exception would change the AAT conclusion or the opinion.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the underlying workpapers.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled reproduction sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Chief Actuary and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Chief Actuary.
